description: §6.7.1a — an `!{}` error-arm inside an `on mount { }` body lowers through the real statement codegen (the same path a `function` body gets), not the string rewriter. `let r = risky() !{ | ::Boom :> "caught" }` — risky() fails with LoadError.Boom; the `:>` recovery arm runs at mount and binds r = "caught"; the two following statements (`@status = r`, `@ran = true`) also run (proving the whole multi-statement body lowered, not just statement 1). Pre-fix this body hit E-CODEGEN-INVALID-LOGIC (the string rewriter cannot lower `!{}`). No input — the boot/mount shape.
rationale: §6.7.1a — `on mount { body }` is sugar for the bare-expression-at-mount pattern; its body MUST lower with the same statement codegen a `function` body uses. An `!{}` guarded call therefore recovers into its binding and subsequent statements execute — exactly as inside a function. The recovery value "caught" (from the ::Boom arm) is r, written into @status; @ran flips true.
